combining DNA-demethylating and histone deacetylation inhibitors in a low-dose regimen can enhance the anti-tumor effects of immune checkpoint therapy in NSCLC.

combining a DNA-demethylating agent (DNA methyltransferases inhibitor [DNMTi]) with a histone deacetylation inhibitor (HDACi) can enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint therapy in non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLCs).

the development of epigenetic therapies to treat lung cancer.
the use of a low-dose sequential combination of DNMTi and HDACi to enhance immune checkpoint therapy for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.
the use of a low-dose, combination epigenetic therapy to reverse tumor immune evasion, and thus enhance immune therapy for NSCLCs.

we have devised a new, sequential, low-dose regimen that enhances immune checkpoint therapy for treating lung cancer.
the combination of DNMTi + HDACi, administered at a low dose, is effective in reversing immune evasion and enhancing immune checkpoint therapy in NSCLC.

epigenetic therapy can be used to reverse tumor immune evasion and treat lung cancer.
